subject: SIG Q12: Clarify data retention for ephemeral GPU / autoscaled pods
messages:

Cc: security@stratagen.com

Subject: SIG Q12 - data retention wording / ephemeral storage clarifications

Hi Mina,

Thanks for sending the SIG earlier this week. Our vendor risk team is reviewing question Q12 (data retention / deletion). The way the question is worded, we're unsure whether you are describing: (a) persistent storage retention (snapshots, backups) or (b) residual data in ephemeral GPU memory or local scratch when autoscaling pods are terminated. The SIG expects a yes/no + explanation, and we need precise language to include in our vendor intake.

Specific asks:
- Do you consider KV cache in GPU memory or local tmpfs ephemeral?
- If a worker is terminated mid-request during autoscaling, is any customer data persisted to node-local disk or snapshots?
- If persistent volumes are used, what are the retention and deletion guarantees for snapshots/backups?

Can we get a written interpretation and any evidence (policy or config) that will satisfy our intake team? If it's easier, happy to schedule a 30 min call.

Best,
Anya
Senior Security Analyst
Stratagen Analytics

Subject: Re: SIG Q12 - data retention wording / ephemeral storage clarifications

Hi Anya — thanks for the clear questions.

Quick summary / proposed interpretation from our side:
- KV cache that lives in GPU DRAM is ephemeral and never persisted to disk by default; it is explicitly cleared on process shutdown.
- We do not write customer request content to host-local disk unless a customer-configured persistent volume (PV) is attached.
- When PVs are used they are encrypted at rest; snapshots and backups follow the retention policy in our retention document.
- Autoscaled worker termination: preStop hooks attempt graceful shutdown to flush checkpoints; if a crash/force-terminate occurs there is no automatic snapshot of GPU memory.

We can provide: a formal interpretation statement for your intake, policy excerpt (retention and snapshot lifecycle), and an architecture diagram of the ephemeral path.

Would a 30-min call tomorrow between 11:00–12:30 PT work to walk through this and capture the exact wording you need? I'm copying Dev (SE) and Evelyn (Security) for technical and control evidence.

Thanks,
Mina
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Subject: Call notes: SIG Q12 - 2026-04-09 11:30 PT (Mina / Dev / Evelyn / Stratagen)

Minutes (agreed on call):
- Attendees: Mina (Redwood), Dev Patel (SE), Evelyn Hart (Security), Anya Koval (Stratagen), +2 from Stratagen intake.
- Agreed interpretation for SIG Q12: "Redwood Inference does not persist customer request payloads in ephemeral compute (GPU/DRAM) or node-local tmpfs beyond request lifecycle. Persistent storage is only used when a customer explicitly mounts a persistent volume; those PVs are encrypted at rest and snapshots are subject to our documented retention policy."
- Autoscaling behavior: preStop hooks attempt graceful cache eviction and flush of any configured checkpoints to PV; forced termination will not produce GPU-memory snapshots.
- Backups/snapshots: automatic snapshots are only taken of customer-attached PVs when configured by the customer; Redwood does not create backups of request payloads outside of customer PVs.
- Deletion/retention windows: snapshots deleted via our UI or API are removed from the snapshot catalog immediately, but underlying provider snapshots may remain in provider retention for up to 48 hours in exceptional cases (we documented processes to request expedited purge).

Action items:
1) Redwood to provide: formal written interpretation (signed by Security), retention policy excerpt, architecture diagram showing ephemeral path, and a short note on provider snapshot purge timeframes.
   - Owner: Evelyn Hart; ETA: 2026-04-10 EOD PT.
2) Stratagen to confirm whether the agreed phrasing satisfies their intake or if legal needs a separate vendor attestation.

Hi Anya — per our call and agreed action items, please find our formal interpretation for SIG Q12 below and links/stubs to evidence. Let us know if you need any additional detail or a signed attestation.

Formal interpretation (to copy into intake):
"Redwood Inference does not persist customer request payloads or model inference inputs in ephemeral GPU memory or node-local temporary files beyond the lifecycle of the request. Persistent storage is only used when explicitly configured by the customer (mounted persistent volumes). Persistent volumes are encrypted at rest, and snapshots/backups of those volumes follow Redwood's documented retention policy; snapshots deleted via the Redwood console or API are removed from the Redwood snapshot catalog immediately, and any underlying cloud-provider snapshot objects are purged within an operational window not to exceed 48 hours under normal circumstances. Redwood does not perform automatic backups of request payloads outside of customer-configured persistent storage."
